messages:
maria: Heads-up — competitor 'Nimbus' just announced 'Adaptive Cost Tiering' (https://nimbus.ai/blog/adaptive-cost-tiering). We should map this to our roadmap: parity, differentiate, or deprioritize? There's a few enterprise asks bubbling in sales. :eyes:
cheng: link, thanks. quick read. main thing looks like a pricing/control UX + routing policy layer. :thinking_face:
noah: scoping Q — is this something we solve in hosting (per-customer policy) or in the runtime (automatic routing & KV cache reuse)?
anya: from product/UX POV this reads as: customers want controls + visibility, not magic models. The UX is a big part of perceived value.
sam: ops take — runtime work for predictive routing is nontrivial. If we reuse the prefix/KV caching infra it's smaller, otherwise 2-3 sprints to a minimum viable routing shim.
maria: Proposal: quick rubric to decide path: 1) demand (reps/customers + revenue signal), 2) eng cost (story points), 3) differentiation (does it block competitors), 4) risk/compliance. Simple score formula:```score = demand*3 - cost*2 + diff*4 - risk*1```Higher -> prioritize.
cheng: can we run a 1-sprint spike to prototype a routing flag + cost calc? I can pick up infra lead if we scope tiny.
noah: Sales signal: ACME + BetaBank specifically asked for per-tenant cost caps and visibility. They said automated tiering would be nice but controls are table stakes. I'll surface exact ARR impact tomorrow.
maria: Decision for now: run a 2-week spike with two arms: (A) parity: shipping basic tiering + admin controls + docs (fast follow), (B) differentiator: predictive routing with auto-savings + rollback policies. Success criteria: >20% token-cost reduction for common seq lengths or clear GTM demand from top 3 accounts. If spike shows high ROI, escalate to Dedicated backlog.
anya: I'll mock flows for both arms and a slim admin console for canary toggles. Deliverables: 3 mocks + interaction notes.
sam: +1. Please include observability events in the spike plan (per-route token breakdown, per-tenant cost deltas) so we can measure impact.
cheng: allocating eng lead. leaning toward reuse of caching + routing layer to cut scope. cc @noah — can you gather the customer ask notes?
noah: On it — scheduling 30m with ACME/Sales tomorrow 10am PST. Will drop notes in the shared doc.
prod-bot: Checklist created: /roadmaps/quickspike-171980 (owners assigned, due in 2w).
maria: Owners: eng=cheng, design=anya, prod-ops=noah, infra=sam. Can we have the spike plan + rough backlog in the shared doc by EOD? https://redwood.docs/roadmaps/quickspike-171980
anya: :thumbsup:
cheng: I'll post a short tech-spec + minimal test matrix by EOD so QA can scope canary tests.
